skill.name: docker-optimizer
skill.description: Reviews Dockerfiles for security, caching, image size, and build quality issues, then suggests optimized Dockerfile and .dockerignore improvements.
skill.summary: Optimize Dockerfiles for smaller, safer, and more reliable container images.
skill.author: CrazyDubya

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline backticks, and illustrative Dockerfile examples. The skill is a documentation-style Dockerfile reviewer with read and edit tools only; no prompt injection, secret exfiltration, or executable command path was found.

remediation.issue: Static analyzers may flag Markdown fences and inline backticks as shell execution.
remediation.suggestion: Keep examples clearly labeled as documentation and avoid ambiguous prose that suggests automatic command execution.

remediation.issue: The example secret can look like a real credential to automated scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Use an obviously fake placeholder such as EXAMPLE_API_KEY_DO_NOT_USE in future examples.

content.value_statement: Dockerfiles often grow large, insecure, and slow to rebuild. This skill helps Claude, Codex, or Claude Code review containers and propose practical optimizations.
actual_capabilities: Finds Dockerfiles and related Dockerfile naming patterns in a project.
Reviews base image tags, layer ordering, and cache efficiency.
Suggests multi-stage builds to reduce final image size.
Checks for common container security issues, including root users and embedded secrets.
Recommends .dockerignore entries to reduce build context and secret exposure.
Provides a Dockerfile checklist for production readiness.
limitations: Does not run Docker builds or image scans by itself.
Does not benchmark actual image size unless the user provides build results.
May need project context to choose the best base image.
Cannot guarantee compatibility for every runtime or package manager.

use_cases.title: Prepare a service for deployment
use_cases.description: Review a Dockerfile before shipping a web service to staging or production.

use_cases.title: Reduce container build time
use_cases.description: Improve layer order and dependency caching for faster CI builds.

use_cases.title: Improve container security posture
use_cases.description: Check for root users, broad COPY patterns, missing cleanup, and secret handling issues.

prompt_templates.title: Review my Dockerfile
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one container file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use docker-optimizer to review my Dockerfile for security, size, and caching issues. Explain the most important changes first.

prompt_templates.title: Create an optimized version
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn an existing Dockerfile into a better production Dockerfile.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use docker-optimizer to rewrite this Dockerfile with a multi-stage build, non-root user, better caching, and a matching .dockerignore.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a repository for Docker issues
prompt_templates.scenario: Review all Dockerfiles in a project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use docker-optimizer to find all Dockerfiles in this repository and summarize the security, size, and build-cache issues in each one.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize CI container builds
prompt_templates.prompt: Use docker-optimizer to improve Docker build performance for CI. Focus on cache reuse, dependency layers, BuildKit, and registry cache strategy.

output_examples.input: Review a Node.js Dockerfile that copies the full repository before installing packages.
output: Move package manifests before source COPY to improve cache reuse.
Use a multi-stage build so development dependencies stay out of the runtime image.
Add a .dockerignore file that excludes node_modules, .git, local env files, and documentation.

output_examples.input: Check whether a Dockerfile is ready for production.
output: Use a specific base image tag instead of latest.
Create and switch to a non-root user before the final command.
Add a health check and remove package manager caches in the same layer.

output_examples.input: Find ways to reduce image size for a Python service.
output: Consider a slim runtime image when Alpine compatibility is uncertain.
Install build tools only in a builder stage.
Copy only application files and installed runtime dependencies into the final image.

best_practices: Provide the Dockerfile, package manager, runtime version, and deployment target together.
Ask for security, size, and cache findings separately when reviewing complex services.
Build and scan the resulting image before production use.
anti_patterns: Do not copy the full repository before installing dependencies unless caching is irrelevant.
Do not bake secrets, tokens, or local environment files into an image.
Do not switch to Alpine without checking native dependency compatibility.

faq.question: Can this skill run Docker commands for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and file edits. Run builds and scans in your own environment.

faq.question: Does it support multi-stage builds?
faq.answer: Yes. It can recommend and draft multi-stage Dockerfiles for smaller runtime images.

faq.question: Can it create a .dockerignore file?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest common exclusions such as dependencies, Git data, local secrets, and documentation.

faq.question: Will it find secrets in existing Dockerfiles?
faq.answer: It checks for common secret patterns, but it is not a full secret scanning replacement.

faq.question: Is it useful for CI performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on layer ordering, dependency caching, BuildKit use, and cache-from strategies.

faq.question: Does it choose the safest base image automatically?
faq.answer: No. It recommends options, but runtime compatibility and organizational policy should guide the final choice.
